The PR replaces raw slice-based truncation of plugin node-invoke approval titles and descriptions with the shared UTF-16-safe truncation helper and adds a focused regression test.

PR surface: Source +1, Tests +21. Total +22 across 2 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Current main uses raw `slice` at the title and description boundaries, and a string with a surrogate pair straddling either boundary deterministically leaves a dangling surrogate.

target.title: fix(gateway): keep plugin approval title and description truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

- AI-assisted; I inspected the changed production path and can explain the change.
- Plugin approval title and description truncation now preserves UTF-16 boundaries at 80 and 256 characters respectively.
- Follows the existing UTF-16-safe truncation hardening pattern.

## Linked context

- No linked issue.
- `String.prototype.slice` cuts at UTF-16 code unit boundaries. Emoji and CJK supplementary characters are surrogate pairs (2 code units). When one straddles the cut position, a lone surrogate is produced that renders as U+FFFD (`�`) in the gateway approval UI payload.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior addressed:** plugin approval requests must not deliver broken surrogates in the `title` or `description` fields of the `PluginApprovalRequestPayload` sent to the gateway approval UI.
- **Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw source checkout on Node v22.22.0; PR head `3d47367617`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts`
  - Standalone `node --import tsx --input-type=module` invocation exercising `truncateUtf16Safe` with a title and description containing emoji at the truncation boundary.
- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts
Test Files  4 passed (4)
     Tests  28 passed (28)
```

Standalone tool-execution transcript from the same head, not a Vitest assertion:

```text
node=v22.22.0
head=3d47367617
fix-title=truncateUtf16Safe
fix-description=truncateUtf16Safe

// Before fix (raw slice) — approval title
title.length=81
slicedTitle.lastCodeUnit=0xd83d
slicedTitle.hasLoneSurrogate=true

// Before fix (raw slice) — approval description
desc.length=257
slicedDesc.lastCodeUnit=0xd83d
slicedDesc.hasLoneSurrogate=true

// After fix (truncateUtf16Safe) — approval title
safeTitle.length=79
safeTitle.matches=true
safeTitle.hasBrokenChar=false

// After fix (truncateUtf16Safe) — approval description
safeDesc.length=255
safeDesc.matches=true
safeDesc.hasBrokenChar=false

// No regression for plain title within limit
truncateUtf16Safe('Install plugin', 80)="Install plugin"
matches-slice=true
```

- **Observed result after fix:** `truncateUtf16Safe` backs out to the last complete character (79 for title, 255 for description), dropping the incomplete surrogate pair. The approval payload never contains a lone surrogate.
- **What was not tested:** full production gateway deployment with an actual plugin executing a dangerous node command was not run; this proof is scoped to the touched approval payload construction path.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** the standalone proof exercises the exact `truncateUtf16Safe` helper used in the production code path. The `PluginApprovalRequestPayload` construction and regression test coverage validate the integration.
- **Before evidence:** `slice(0, 80)` on a string with an emoji at position 80-81 leaves a high surrogate (0xD83D) without its low-surrogate pair, rendering as U+FFFD in the approval UI.

## Tests and validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/node-invoke-plugin-policy.test.ts`
- Added focused regression test: "does not cut approval title with an emoji straddling the truncation boundary" — verifies the high surrogate at position 79 and proves truncateUtf16Safe produces clean output.
- No known local failures from this change.

## Risk checklist

**Did user-visible behavior change? (Yes/No)**

Yes. Approval UI payloads that would previously contain a dangling surrogate character now deliver cleanly truncated text.

**Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (Yes/No)**

No.

**Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (Yes/No)**

No.

**What is the highest-risk area?**

Gateway approval request payload formatting for plugin node.invoke policies.

**How is that risk mitigated?**

The patch is limited to the two existing truncation boundaries in `createApprovalRuntime`, uses the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper that is already battle-tested across 16+ other code paths, preserves the existing caps (80/256), and is covered by a focused regression test plus standalone tool execution proof.
